Also read the actual component source: components-legacy/ui/ImageFallback.tsx (full file), app/api/salons/[slug]/gallery/route.ts, app/api/reviews/[id]/photos/route.ts, app/api/services/[id]/photos/route.ts, app/api/clients/[id]/photos/route.ts, next.config.mjs images block. Ran greps across the repo for: next/image import count (33) vs raw count (35, listed by file), sizes= (34) and priority (12) prop usage, alt= usage (92 total, 55 are alt=""), onError fallback wiring, sharp/exif/EXIF package or code presence (zero hits), moderation-related files (found app/api/admin/discovery/moderation/route.ts for discovery content only, no equivalent for salon-gallery or review photos), object-position usage (2 hits, one taste-log-approved one-off on SalonImageGallery only), loading="lazy" (9 hits) and placeholder="blur" (0 hits), storage bucket names in use (avatars, client-photos, discovery-images, review-photos, salon-documents, service-photos, salon-gallery), and consent/rights-checkbox language near upload components (none found). Cross-checked every candidate against REMOVED.md and TASTE_LOG.md before writing it up; only one adjacent graveyard hit (TikTok's own player embed rejected for /entdecken, explicitly distinguished in the same REMOVED.md line from 'real inline player ONLY for owned/salon video (we have the file)' i.e. salon-owned video was anticipated, not rejected).

findings.title: No EXIF/GPS metadata stripping on any photo upload path
findings.principle: Every image uploaded by a user (salon gallery, review photo, service photo, client progress photo, profile avatar) must have EXIF metadata, including GPS coordinates and device identifiers, stripped server-side before the file is written to Storage or served publicly. No uploaded image byte stream reaches a public bucket unprocessed.
findings.why: A phone photo carries GPS coordinates and device metadata by default. A salon owner uploading a gallery photo from their own phone (at home, before opening the shop) or a customer uploading a review photo can unknowingly publish their home address or device fingerprint to a public bucket that anyone can download and inspect. This is a live privacy leak from day one of public launch, not a hypothetical.
findings.local_evidence: Read app/api/salons/[slug]/gallery/route.ts, app/api/reviews/[id]/photos/route.ts, app/api/services/[id]/photos/route.ts, app/api/clients/[id]/photos/route.ts end to end: every one of the four upload routes does `formData.get("file")` -> MIME/size check -> `supabase.storage.from(<bucket>).upload(path, file)` directly. No `sharp`, no `exif`, no metadata-stripping step anywhere in the call chain. `grep -n '"sharp"' package.json` returns nothing; the package is not even a dependency.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'exif' across _design-system, _rules, _docs, CLAUDE.md, _backend-system, ~/.claude/*.md, ~/.claude/hooks: zero hits anywhere. grep -ri 'strip.*metadata' and 'gps' in the same set: zero hits. The concept does not exist in the law estate at all, not even as an open question in QUESTIONS.md.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/PHOTO_STRATEGY.md (new section: upload pipeline) plus _rules/ (a new or existing security/privacy rules file), enforced in a shared lib/media/process-upload.ts helper all four upload routes call.
findings.enforcement: gate: a lib helper `stripImageMetadata(buffer)` that every upload route must call before `.upload()`; a static grep gate could flag any `storage.from(...).upload(` call in app/api that does not pass through the shared helper first.

findings.title: No pre-publish moderation for salon-gallery or review photos, unlike Discovery content
findings.principle: Any customer- or salon-owner-uploaded photo that will render on a public page (salon gallery, review photo) is queued for moderation before going live, using the same moderation primitive already built for Discovery content, or is at minimum passed through an automated NSFW/violence classifier synchronously at upload time; it is never inserted straight into a public-read table with no gate.
findings.why: A marketplace that lets any authenticated salon owner or reviewer publish an image straight to a public URL with zero review is one inappropriate upload away from a trust and safety incident once real users are live. The existing reactive-only tools (ban a user after the fact, flag a review after the fact) only catch the problem after the image has already been publicly served, possibly indexed, and possibly screenshotted.
findings.local_evidence: app/api/salons/[slug]/gallery/route.ts POST inserts into `salon-gallery` storage and updates `salons.gallery_urls` with no status/is_hidden/moderation_status column touched at all (grep for those column names in the file returns nothing). app/api/reviews/[id]/photos/route.ts is identical: uploads to `review-photos` then a plain INSERT into `review_photos`, immediately visible on the PDP reviews section (per _docs/FRONTEND.md:1031-1037, 'Add/remove up to 3 photos... photo POST /api/reviews/[id]/photos as FormData after review id returns — REAL'). By contrast app/api/admin/discovery/moderation/route.ts exists as a dedicated moderation surface for Discovery items, proving the team already has the pattern and simply never extended it to owner-uploaded and reviewer-uploaded photos.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'moderat' over _design-system, _rules, _docs, CLAUDE.md, _backend-system: every hit is either Discovery-scoped (admin/discovery/moderation) or generic report/flag endpoints (reviews/[id]/flag, admin/reports) that act AFTER a review is already public. No hit describes a pre-publish gate for salon_portfolio_images or review_photos.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: Discovery content has a moderation admin page (app/api/admin/discovery/moderation/route.ts); salon gallery photos and review photos have only a post-hoc report/flag/ban mechanism, not a pre-publish gate.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/PHOTO_STRATEGY.md (moderation section) + _rules/ (trust-and-safety rule), backed by extending the existing discovery-moderation admin surface to cover salon_portfolio_images and review_photos.
findings.enforcement: gate: a DB check (moderation_status column + RLS predicate `moderation_status = 'approved'` on the public SELECT policy) so an unmoderated row physically cannot render on the PDP even if the code forgets to filter it.

findings.title: Alt text has no authoring rule and is empty on informative content images
findings.principle: Every image tag decides, at write time, whether it is decorative (alt="" is correct) or informative (alt must describe the depicted content, never just repeat the salon name that is already visible as text next to it). A content photo the user can open, save, or scroll through (portfolio grid tile, saved-salon tile, gallery swipe photo) always carries a real alt describing what the photo shows; only chrome/icon-glyph images get alt="".
findings.why: A screen-reader user browsing a photo-heavy portfolio grid or a saved-salons tile grid currently hears nothing at all for every tile, because the image is the only element in that tile (no adjacent text label). That is not decoration hidden correctly, it is content hidden by omission, which fails WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.1.1 (Non-text Content) for every one of those images.
findings.local_evidence: Measured: `grep -rn 'alt='` returns 92 hits, of which 55 are literally `alt=""` (grep -rn 'alt=""'). Concretely: app/[locale]/_components/salon/SalonPortfolio.tsx:123 `` for a portfolio tile the user taps to open in a lightbox (this IS the content, not decoration); app/[locale]/_components/profile/ProfileTabs.tsx:337,360,370,377 uses `alt=""` on every saved-salon and past-booking tile photo in the profile hub; app/[locale]/queue/[token]/page.tsx:354 uses `alt=""` on the swipeable salon-photo gallery in the live walk-in tracker (described in _docs/FRONTEND.md:526 as 'the single largest element on the screen'). Compare to app/[locale]/_components/primitives/Avatar.tsx:74 which correctly uses `alt={name}` on the identical img pattern, proving the inconsistency is a missing rule, not a universal choice.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'alt.text\|alt=\|aria-label' over _design-system/LOCKFILE.md, SOURCE.md, COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md, and _rules/: zero hits describing when alt should be empty vs descriptive, or what a descriptive alt must contain. _rules/ has no accessibility file at all covering images specifically.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/SOURCE.md (accessibility section, a11y) with a decision rule (decorative vs informative), and a line item in this domain's future PHOTO_STRATEGY.md.
findings.enforcement: checklist item in the design-verifier scorecard (SENIOR_SCORECARD.md) that greps a screen's rendered DOM for img/Image tags with alt="" that sit inside a tappable/openable element (a strong signal of wrongly-decorative-tagged content).

findings.title: 35 raw tags on customer surfaces bypass next/image, including the locked global Avatar primitive
findings.principle: Every image whose src the app controls (any Supabase Storage URL, any remote allowlisted host) renders through next/image, never a raw , on any customer-facing route. A raw is permitted only for content next/image structurally cannot handle (HTML email templates, or a data: URI generated client-side).
findings.why: next/image is the only mechanism in this codebase that gives automatic responsive srcset generation, format negotiation, and lazy-loading by default. A raw gets none of that: it ships the full-resolution original at every viewport width, which directly works against the imagery floor (LOCKFILE + CLAUDE.md require photos to be ~1/3 of the customer viewport) by making the heaviest-imagery screens also the least optimized ones.
findings.local_evidence: grep -rn ': SalonPortfolio.tsx:123, SalonImageGallery.tsx:232, ProfileTabs.tsx (5 instances), queue/[token]/page.tsx (3 instances), RecentlyViewedClient.tsx, walk-in-pay/page.tsx, inspo/page.tsx, inspo/board/[id]/page.tsx, and critically primitives/Avatar.tsx:74 -- the ONE component COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md calls 'the canonical avatar for any person/salon avatar' and lists as used at 5+ production call-sites (reviews, staff carousel, staff profile) -- meaning every staff and reviewer photo across the whole product ships unoptimized.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'next/image\|raw img\|' over _design-system/LOCKFILE.md, SOURCE.md, COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md: no rule mandating next/image usage or banning raw anywhere. LOCKFILE's imagery section (S11, line ~1130) covers aspect ratios, radius, and the 5 content patterns, but never states which HTML mechanism must render them.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/SOURCE.md or LOCKFILE.md (new imagery-implementation rule) plus a lint/drift-check rule (solen-drift-check already scans for other component-usage drift, this is the same shape of check).
findings.enforcement: gate: extend the existing `solen-drift-check` skill / pre-edit-drift-gate.sh to flag any new `

findings.title: The documented grey-box fallback and the shipped fallback component describe two different visuals
findings.principle: The imagery fallback recipe stated in CLAUDE.md ('fallback = sunken bg + category icon + initial') must be the literal, single, current description of what ImageFallback.tsx renders. When the shipped component changes, the same turn updates every doc row describing it; a fallback recipe is never allowed to exist as two different descriptions in two different places.
findings.why: An engineer or agent reading CLAUDE.md's imagery row and building against 'sunken bg + category icon + initial' will produce a mockup or code path that doesn't match what actually renders in production, and the design-verifier will grade against whichever description it happens to read, silently passing a screen that contradicts the other document.
findings.local_evidence: CLAUDE.md line 67 and the design-contract imagery row (line 92) both state the missing-photo fallback is 'sunken bg + category icon + initial'. The actual shipped component, components-legacy/ui/ImageFallback.tsx (read in full), renders something categorically different: a solid saturated per-category HEX color block (amber #D4870A for coiffeur, plum #4A1E3C for barber, coral #E8624A for nails, etc, defined lines 31-41) with the salon's first name-word in giant uppercase Anton lettering (clamp 32-56px) centered on top -- no sunken bg, no category icon, no initial. The component's own comment at line 8-11 says 'we are NOT using uploaded photos on cards -- every salon card image is a solid per-category color block', confirming this is the intentional current design, just never reconciled with the CLAUDE.md wording.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n 'sunken.*icon.*initial\|category icon.*initial' CLAUDE.md _design-system/*.md: only the two CLAUDE.md hits above; grep -n 'ImageFallback\|per-category color\|solid color block' CLAUDE.md _design-system/LOCKFILE.md: zero hits, meaning the actual shipped recipe (per-category solid color + name label) has NO home in the law estate at all, it lives only in a code comment.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: CLAUDE.md states a fallback recipe, but it describes a different visual than what ships; the actual shipped recipe is undocumented outside a component-file comment.
findings.where_it_should_live: CLAUDE.md imagery row + _design-system/LOCKFILE.md imagery section, corrected to match the shipped component (or the component corrected to match the law, whichever the owner picks).
findings.enforcement: doc-only (a one-line correction), but flag to the owner explicitly since it is a live contradiction, not a gap.

findings.title: No image weight (KB) budget or compression pipeline for user-uploaded photos
findings.principle: Every image accepted from a salon owner or customer is re-encoded server-side to a bounded maximum file size (for example, 300KB at the largest served dimension) before it is written to Storage, independent of the raw upload's original size. The 5MB upload cap is an INPUT ceiling, not a served-weight guarantee.
findings.why: The upload routes only cap the ORIGINAL file at 5MB; nothing re-encodes or compresses it afterward. A phone photo at or near that 5MB ceiling, uploaded through a raw tag (finding imagery-icons-04) with no next/image optimization layer, is served to every visitor at its original weight. On a photo-heavy marketplace where the imagery floor requires photos to cover roughly a third of every viewport, this compounds directly into slow LCP and real mobile data cost for Swiss users on limited plans.
findings.local_evidence: app/api/salons/[slug]/gallery/route.ts, app/api/reviews/[id]/photos/route.ts, app/api/services/[id]/photos/route.ts, app/api/clients/[id]/photos/route.ts all cap `file.size > 5 * 1024 * 1024` and then upload the file object AS-IS to Storage with no intermediate processing step; no `sharp`, `imagemin`, or Cloudinary transform call exists anywhere in the codebase (confirmed by the same absence-of-sharp grep as finding 01). _design-system/SOURCE.md:830 only has a soft note ('Lazy-load below-fold images -- already default for next/image but worth confirming'), which is an unverified aspiration, not a locked number.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'kb budget\|image weight\|compress\|imagemin\|tinypng\|cloudinary' over _design-system, _rules, _docs, CLAUDE.md, package.json: zero hits for any compression tool or a stated weight ceiling. PHOTO_STRATEGY.md explicitly rejects Cloudinary as a vendor (line 10) but names no replacement compression step for user uploads, only for the 6 static AI-generated hero images (which ARE pre-optimized per line 8: '1600w + 800w AVIF/WebP').
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the 6 static category-hero images ARE pre-sized AVIF/WebP per PHOTO_STRATEGY.md section 1, but every dynamic salon/review/client photo (the overwhelming majority of images actually served, per the density floor requiring PDP gallery >= 5 photos and reviews >= 3 photos per salon) has no equivalent treatment.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/PHOTO_STRATEGY.md (new 'dynamic upload pipeline' section), a shared lib/media processing helper called from every upload route.
findings.enforcement: gate: same shared upload-processing helper as finding imagery-icons-01 (metadata strip + re-encode + weight cap in one pass); measurable via a Lighthouse/LCP budget check on the PDP and homepage in CI.

findings.title: No rights/consent attestation at photo upload time for salon-gallery or review photos
findings.principle: Any upload flow that publishes a photo of a real place or a real person (salon gallery, review photo depicting staff or other clients) requires the uploader to affirmatively confirm they own the rights to the image or have the depicted person's consent, at the moment of upload, logged with a timestamp. This binds salon owners and customers equally; it is not satisfied by a Terms of Service clause nobody reads.
findings.why: A review photo can depict a staff member's face or another customer without their knowledge; a salon gallery photo could be lifted from a competitor's Instagram. Once real customers are live, an unconsented photo of a real person or a copyright claim on a scraped photo becomes the platform's legal exposure, and there is currently zero UI moment that makes the uploader pause and confirm anything.
findings.local_evidence: app/api/salons/[slug]/gallery/route.ts and app/api/reviews/[id]/photos/route.ts both go straight from `formData.getAll("photos")`/`formData.get("file")` to a Storage `.upload()` call with no rights/consent field read or recorded anywhere in either route (confirmed by reading both files in full, no `consent`, `rights`, `license`, or `attestation` field referenced). grep for consent-adjacent language near the gallery upload UI (app/[locale]/_components/salon/) turns up only the unrelated cookie-consent banner.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'rights\|licens\|copyright\|consent' _design-system/PHOTO_STRATEGY.md, LOCKFILE.md, CLAUDE.md, _rules/, _backend-system/: the only hits are PHOTO_STRATEGY.md lines 15-16, and those cover ONLY the 6 owner-approved AI-generated category-hero images ('Google's generated-content terms permit commercial use... confirm current Gemini image terms before public launch') plus a stock-photo fallback note. Zero coverage of salon-owner uploads or customer review-photo uploads, which are the vast majority of live images.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: rights/licensing is addressed for the 6 static AI hero images only; the dynamic, much larger volume of salon-gallery and review photos has no equivalent language anywhere.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/PHOTO_STRATEGY.md (new 'user-generated content rights' section) plus the upload UI copy (an inline checkbox or affirmation line above the upload button).
findings.enforcement: checklist / behavioral rule (a UI copy requirement, not code-testable beyond confirming the checkbox/copy exists and is required before the upload button enables).

findings.title: No general face-safe crop rule; the one fix that exists is scoped to a single component
findings.principle: Any photo of a person (avatar, staff carousel, review photo, salon hero photo that may include a person) that is force-cropped by aspect ratio uses a face-aware or top-weighted crop position (object-position: top, or a computed focal point), never the CSS default center crop, unless the source has been pre-cropped square by the uploader.
findings.why: A center crop on a portrait-oriented source, forced into a landscape or square frame, systematically cuts off the top of a person's head, which is the single most noticeable image-quality defect a user will spot on a staff or avatar photo. The team has already found and fixed this once in one place; the fix was never generalized.
findings.local_evidence: TASTE_LOG.md line 326 records a settled, owner-approved decision: 'ig4 dp-crop-bone-shaft-not-joint | APPROVED | gallery uploader gets one framing line; square photo grid crops center-top, not blind center', implemented at app/[locale]/_components/salon/SalonImageGallery.tsx:245-247 (`object-cover object-top`, with a code comment explicitly noting 'was center'). grep -rn 'object-position\|object-top' across app/components/lib returns exactly 2 hits, both in that one file (plus its /dev/ overhaul mirror). Every other person-photo crop in the codebase (Avatar.tsx line 74, SalonHero.tsx galleries, SalonTeam.tsx staff carousel, SalonResultCard.tsx, CategoryHeroCarousel.tsx) uses plain `object-cover` with the CSS default center position.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'face.*crop\|focal point\|smart crop\|object-position' over _design-system/LOCKFILE.md, SOURCE.md, COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md: zero hits describing a general rule; the only trace of the concept is the single TASTE_LOG.md line above, scoped by its own wording to 'the gallery uploader' and 'square photo grid', not to Avatar or any other person-photo component.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: a settled, dated decision exists (TASTE_LOG ig4) but it is scoped to one component (SalonImageGallery's uploader grid); it was never generalized into a LOCKFILE rule covering Avatar, SalonHero, SalonTeam, or any other person-photo crop.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md imagery section (S11), generalizing ig4 into a named rule with the component list it applies to.
findings.enforcement: checklist item in the design-verifier for any new person-photo crop; long-term, a computed focal-point (simple face-detection at upload time storing a focal y-offset) would make this measurable rather than a manual object-position guess.

findings.title: No stated policy for salon-uploaded video, despite the team having already anticipated it
findings.principle: Salon-owner-uploaded video (of the salon space, a haircut, a treatment) follows a named, written policy covering: allowed formats/codecs, a duration and file-size ceiling, where in the PDP it may appear relative to the photo gallery, and whether it counts toward or is exempt from the imagery-floor photographic-area measurement. Until that policy exists, no salon video upload path may ship.
findings.why: The team has already flagged this as a real near-term feature (not a hypothetical): REMOVED.md's TikTok-embed rejection entry explicitly carves out an exception for 'real inline player ONLY for owned/salon video (we have the file)', meaning owned salon video was treated as a planned, different feature at the time the TikTok player was rejected. Shipping that feature later with no governing spec risks re-litigating the same aspect-ratio, autoplay, and imagery-floor questions the rest of this domain already answered for photos.
findings.local_evidence: REMOVED.md line 32 (TikTok inline embed rejection): 'Static hero + tap-to-open is the call; real inline player ONLY for owned/salon video (we have the file)'. LOCKFILE.md line 1148 states 'No <video> on marketing surfaces... Uber's 8 surfaces use zero. Stills + Lottie illustrations only. (Carve-out: /entdecken TikTok-stream feature exempt)' -- this rule covers MARKETING surfaces and the Discovery feed only; it says nothing about the PDP, which is a transactional/booking surface, not marketing, so the existing no-video rule doesn't even technically reach the salon-video case the graveyard entry anticipated.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'salon video\|owned video\|video upload\|video policy' over _design-system, _rules, _docs, CLAUDE.md: the single REMOVED.md hit above is the only trace of the concept; no PHOTO_STRATEGY.md, LOCKFILE.md, or COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md section addresses it. review photo upload explicitly rejects video mime types (jpeg/png/webp allowlist) but this is never framed as a stated video-exclusion policy for reviews specifically, just an incidental byproduct of the allowlist.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: LOCKFILE.md's no-video-on-marketing rule exists but is scoped to marketing surfaces + the Discovery carve-out; it does not reach the PDP/salon-gallery case the graveyard entry names as a real anticipated feature.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/PHOTO_STRATEGY.md (new 'salon video' section, written BEFORE the feature is built, per this project's own build-self-test-then-integrate discipline).
findings.enforcement: doc-only until the feature is built; then a mockup-first gate per the standard mockup-first law.

findings.title: No LQIP/placeholder strategy for below-the-fold photo grids, only an explicit ban for the above-fold hero
findings.principle: Every photo grid or masonry feed that loads more images than fit in the first viewport (PDP portfolio grid, Inspo masonry feed, saved-tiles grid) renders a neutral sunken-color placeholder box at the image's final aspect ratio while the image loads, so the layout never shifts and the tile is never a blank white flash. This is distinct from and does not contradict the existing rule that the ABOVE-FOLD hero photo must NOT use a lingering blur-up placeholder.
findings.why: The team correctly identified that a blur-up placeholder on the single most important above-fold photo (PDP hero, queue-tracker gallery) delays the 100ms trust-forming first impression and banned it there. But that finding was never balanced with a floor for the opposite case: a masonry feed or portfolio grid with a dozen images below the fold has nothing filling the gap while images stream in, which is the layout-shift and blank-flash problem the placeholder pattern exists to solve, on exactly the surfaces (Inspo, PDP gallery) this domain's density floor requires to be image-dense.
findings.local_evidence: PSYCH_AUDIT_2026-07-07.md:524-526 documents the hero decision as 'GOOD' explicitly: 'Live tracker leads with a large real photo hero... falls back to a plain neutral fill... when no photos exist (not a lingering blur-up placeholder)'. `grep -rn 'placeholder="blur"'` across app/components/lib returns 0 hits anywhere in the codebase, meaning the below-fold case was never implemented either, not even where it would help (SalonPortfolio 3-col grid up to 9 tiles, Inspo MasonryGrid). SkeletonCard (COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md line 31) covers the loading STATE for a whole card before any data arrives, but not the per-image pop-in inside an already-rendered grid once data is present and images are still streaming.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'lqip\|blur.up\|blur placeholder\|pop.in\|layout shift' over _design-system, _rules, _docs, CLAUDE.md: only the single PSYCH_AUDIT hit above (hero-scoped, explicitly praising the ABSENCE of blur there); no hit anywhere addresses the below-fold grid case.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the hero case is explicitly and correctly locked (no blur placeholder above the fold); the below-fold grid case, which is the more common surface given the density floor, is simply unaddressed.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/PHOTO_STRATEGY.md (new section distinguishing hero vs grid loading treatment) or SOURCE.md's loading-states section alongside SkeletonCard.
findings.enforcement: checklist item for the design-verifier when reviewing any new photo grid/masonry surface; measurable via Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) on the Inspo feed and PDP portfolio in Lighthouse.
